text:
emma_sales: Quick heads-up: BioHealth wants a 48h POC to connect their on‑prem app to our Private API. Which path is faster to stand up for them (VPCE vs VPC peering)? Can we also provide a short smoke API key for curl tests?

ravi_se: VPCE (interface endpoint) is usually quickest and requires minimal changes on our side. Checklist: private subnets in 2 AZs, SG that allows outbound 443 from their app to the VPCE ENIs, and enable Private DNS on the endpoint so SDKs resolve our private host. We can issue an ephemeral token (8–12h) scoped to the POC. Example snippets below.

nora_infra: Peering is doable but slower: non‑overlapping CIDRs, create+accept pcx, update route tables both sides, no automatic Private DNS. If they already have a VPN/TGW, VPCE still works behind that but watch DNS forwarding.

ravi_se: VPCE create (customer runs):
```bash
aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint \\n  --vpc-id vpc-0abc123 \\n  --service-name com.amazonaws.vpce.us-west-2.vpce-svc-xxxx \\n  --vpc-endpoint-type Interface \\n  --subnet-ids subnet-aaa subnet-bbb \\n  --security-group-ids sg-0a1b2c3 \
  --private-dns-enabled
```
Test curl (use ephemeral token):
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <EPHEMERAL>" https://private-api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/healthz
```
Expect 200 {"status":"ok"}.

sam_sec: Security: do NOT use org-wide long-lived keys for POCs. Approve ephemeral tokens only. If they require mTLS, thatadds setup time (~2 business days). Also ask for their egress/NAT plan so we can confirm control plane access.

infra_bot: Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/privatelink-quick-poc contains SG templates and DNS troubleshooting steps.

emma_sales: Action items: (1) ravi_se prepare ephemeral token flow + README (today), (2) nora_infra send VPCE CLI & SG example to customer (ASAP), (3) sam_sec send minimal security checklist and mTLS note. I'll schedule kickoff once they confirm subnets. Thanks!
